extracted.intended_audience: health journalists, health-news consumers, and organizations producing or evaluating health news
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and standards for evaluating news stories about medical treatments, tests, products, and procedures — emphasizing accuracy, balance, and completeness and providing consumers tools to evaluate evidence. Includes the site's star-rating approach and expectations of objectivity/unbiased presentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accuracy
rubrics_metrics.description: Accuracy (one of the 'ABCs of health journalism').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the site: 'Improving the accuracy of news stories about medical treatments, tests, products and procedures.' The site exists to promote accurate reporting of medical information and to critique stories for factual correctness and faithful representation of study results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance (one of the 'ABCs of health journalism').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the site's stated focus: helping consumers evaluate the evidence for and against new ideas in health care. Implies that coverage should present both supporting and opposing evidence/interpretations rather than one-sided claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: Completeness (one of the 'ABCs of health journalism').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site emphasizes completeness of reporting so that consumers have enough information to evaluate the story — linked to the Foundation's objective to 'organize and frame medical evidence in an unbiased manner to help people evaluate their options.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Organize and frame medical evidence in an unbiased manner
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether reporting organizes and frames the medical evidence without bias so readers can evaluate options.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit guidance from the Foundation: 'Organize and frame medical evidence in an unbiased manner to help people evaluate their options, particularly in cases where differences in individual preferences and perspectives are likely to affect personal choice.' This encompasses presenting study context, limitations, absolute vs relative risks, and alternative explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Help consumers evaluate evidence for and against new ideas in health care
rubrics_metrics.description: Assess whether the story helps consumers weigh evidence supporting and opposing new treatments, tests, products, or procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated mission: 'Helping consumers evaluate the evidence for and against new ideas in health care.' Guidance implies reviewers look for presentation of comparative evidence, magnitude of benefit/harm, study quality, and practical implications for patients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide information that is objective, complete and unbiased
rubrics_metrics.description: Stories (and the site's own materials) should strive to be objective, complete, and unbiased.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: From the Foundation's aims: 'The Foundation provides information that is as objective, complete and unbiased as possible' in contexts where cost savings, commercial interests or professional beliefs may influence decisions. Reviewers therefore assess commercial/professional conflicts of interest, promotional tone, and selective presentation of results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Star score (0–5) rating/searchability
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of a 0–5 star system to rate stories and allow searching by review rating.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site provides a star-rating system (0–5) — users may search reviews by entering '0 - 5 star' (e.g., '3 star' or '1 star'). The site menu also references 'How is the Star Score Determined', indicating an underlying scoring rubric that maps review criteria to a star score.
